picks.catalyst: Gap down: selling Mailchimp at a big loss + trimmed full-year sales forecast (quarter itself beat)
picks.why: Intuit beat on its quarter but agreed to sell Mailchimp for about $3.68B (it paid about $12B) and nudged its yearly sales forecast down to $23.08B-$23.37B, so it's down about 10% before the open; this hurts sentiment, not the business's survival, so a big name like this can bounce once early sellers are done. Wait for the desk's trigger, and remember the whole market is weak today.

picks.catalyst: Gap down: beat and raised the year, but holiday-quarter profit forecast a bit light
picks.why: Ross had a strong quarter (sales up 12%, profit $1.91 a share vs. its own $1.75-$1.83 plan) and raised its full-year forecast, but its holiday-quarter profit range ($2.16-$2.25) came in a little under hopes, so it's down roughly 3-4%; a good business dipping on a small guidance miss is a classic 'can reverse' setup. No reliable pre-market price found, so use the live quote.

picks.catalyst: Sector sell-off (AI chips/memory) - no Micron-specific bad news
picks.why: Micron is down about 5% only because chip stocks are being sold across the board after a rough night in Asia and a UBS note on AI spending pressure, not because of anything Micron reported; sector-wide drops like this can reverse, but only trade it if the chip group stops falling after the open.
